english: the bigger they come, the harder they fall
also: the higher they climb, the harder they fall

evidence: Publil. Sent. E 16 (loci collection; Pub. Syr. 162 Ribbeck in Lewis & Short s.v. excellō)
terms.comment: Literally “a fall hurts those on high far more easily”: a line of Publilius Syrus.
Traupman’s rewording of Publilius’s line, with the singular excelsī, “a fall from on high”.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Publilius Syrus, Sententiae E 16, as numbered in the Latīnitās loci collection, checked against the Latin Library texts (CLTK mirror) (12 November 2026).
Publilius is cited as the loci collection numbers him, by position under each initial letter in the Latin Library text.
